correctness.rationale: For every n in {2,3,4,5,6,7}, the induced cyclic-11-free graph is reconstructed directly. Identifying signatures are equivalent to hitting each nonempty closed neighborhood and each pairwise symmetric difference of closed neighborhoods. Since the property is upward closed, exhaustive exclusion at I_n-1 proves no smaller code exists; exhaustive counts at I_n prove exact minima and populations. At n=7 there are exactly C(29,10)=20,030,010 and C(29,11)=34,597,290 tested subsets; zero and 259 pass respectively. The dihedral group action is checked as a vertex permutation and all minimum codes are partitioned into complete orbits. Full-invariant codes are exhaustively enumerated as unions of dihedral vertex-orbits, giving unique 8-sensor n=6 layout and precisely three 14-sensor n=7 layouts. Two independently implemented C++17 algorithms, one testing exact hitting-mask constraints and one direct signatures, reproduced every row, including orbit-size multisets, and printed VERIFY_OK and ALTERNATE_OK. The exact witnesses in CENSUS.json and direct signature check agree. No claim beyond n=7 is inferred.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Lucas domination gamma <= identifying-code number, but a lower domination bound cannot in general establish that identifying-code number is 7 at n6 and 11 at n7; packing equality/nonequality is also insufficient. Graph vertex-orbits determine allowable invariant unions, but not which identify all vertices. Lack of perfect error-correcting codes forbids a disjoint ball partition, not identification by overlapping signatures. The new computational exact results and 259-code enumeration require independent complete finite testing, not immediate corollaries of prior publications.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Identifying-code feasibility requires every radius-one vertex signature be nonempty AND pairwise distinct. A dominating set enforces only the first property; a 2-packing requires disjoint balls, not unique nonempty intersections. Edge-color observability is a different graph invariant. These related statements are not equivalent and do not fix the enumerated optimum placements.

originality.rationale: The assessed advance is the exact identification-code and full-dihedral-invariance classification of Lucas cubes for n=2..7, with the first one-sensor dihedral penalty at six positions, three-sensor penalty at seven, and complete 259-placement/23-symmetry-class census at n=7. Closest sources establish other graph parameters, general identification formulations or vertex-orbit symmetries, none of which mathematically implies this particular minimum-and-equality classification. Direct and alias literature and indexed-record searches found no exact or stronger covering statement. Historical priority remains qualified because non-indexed computations might exist.

value.rationale: Full-coordinate rotation/reflection invariance is a natural network deployment constraint on cyclically defined Lucas graphs. The first dimension requiring an extra identifying sensor (6) and the three-extra-sensor requirement at dimension seven quantify nontrivial symmetry costs, not just a routine restatement of dominating sets. The exact population 259 and its twenty-three distinct dihedral symmetry types, together with three fully invariant fourteen-sensor equality cases, form a complete nontrivial and reproducible equality classification and benchmark. Graphs have up to 29 vertices so the finite exhaustive computation is genuinely self-contained. No unproved extrapolation or paper-sized downstream application is claimed.
